recipes.name: Salmon with Brown Sugar and Bourbon Glaze

steps.text: Melt butter in a large heavy skillet over medium heat. Stir in brown sugar. Place salmon fillets on top of brown sugar mixture. Cook for 5 minutes on medium heat. Turn salmon, and pour bourbon around the fillets. Continue cooking for 5 minutes, or until fish flakes easily with a fork. Spoon glaze over the salmon, and serve.

review.reviewBody: This is a recipe I also use and get rave reviews over. However....I adapted it 3 yrs ago from TX Land and Cattle restaurant's version, only they use brown sugar and Shiner Bock dark beer! With this bourbon version, I lay my fillets out and gently press the brown sugar into the fillets, then sprinkle them with the bourbon - I let them "rest" for about 30 minutes before quickly browning the sugar glazed filets over med-high heat in a non-stick saucepan, about 2 min each side. I wrap up the cooking process by popping them in the microwave for 1-1 1/2 minutes, depending on the thickness of the filets. These filets make a terrific presentation in a romaine-based salad with a topping of honey and brown sugar glazed coarsely chopped pecans (Johnny Carino's restaurants serve it like this) Enjoy! Impressive and will work well over the holidays.

This was delicious and fast and easy to make. I tweaked it a little: as a reviewer suggested, I sprinkled brown sugar on the salmon before cooking it, but used only about 1 Tbsp of sugar for 4 fillets. I then mixed about 3 Tbsps of low sodium soy sauce, the juice of half a lemon, 1/2 tsp of honey, and 1 shot of bourbon, and sprinkled a little on each fillet. I let the fish sit for about 20 mins, then pan fried it 2 mins. each side (the fillets were thin). When the fish was ready, I took it out of the pan, and put in the rest of the sauce, boiling it until it thickened. I poured this over the fish and served it with rice and asparagus. Delicious!

I only had light brown sugar so added a little molasses. Really liked the additional molasses and will add a little regardless of what kind of brown sugar I have on hand. 

Cooking time of the salmon needs to be adjusted for thickness of your fish. 5 minutes is too long for the salmon pieces I had.

This sauce would be good by itself on ice cream!

I make this frequently and it works well on stove top but do be careful not to burn the glaze. Another option that is wonderful is to place the glaze with the bourbon or whiskey mixed in into a foil tent. Place the salmon in the foil and spoon the glaze over. Grill on medium heat for about 5 minutes. Amazing!

We both thought that the sauce was too sweet. If I made it again, I would add something in or cut the brown sugar down to at least 1/3 c.

Letting the sauce thicken more might've also helped. With such a short cooking time, the sauce was still pretty thin. Next time I would remove the salmon and continue cooking the sauce.

Fabulous recipe that is quick to prepare, to say the least, and delivers phenomenal flavor. DEBOKC knocked the ball out of the park. 

The Bourbon and brown sugar combination is magic. I made the recipe exactly as instructed, but I wondered about adding some seasoning; the Bourbon and brown sugar starts to sound like a grilling recipe, so I added a sprinkle of garlic powder and onion powder, as well as a little ground kosher salt and ground Tellicherry pepper.

I'll comment on the one-star rating that this recipe received about burning the sugar: *Don't* go off and do something on the internet while this is cooking, as you wouldn't ignore other sautés that you do. Also, feel free to adjust the flame or power to lower as it cooks, if necessary. If the heat is high, you have plenty of time to adjust it, long before the sugar would burn.

When you sample the sauce, you'll know that you have reached satori, as we might say. Butter, brown sugar and Bourbon is to die for. And it does so much for that salmon!

so good! I added the brown sugar, salt and pepper before cooking them. also added the brown sugar to the butter as instructed. I only cooked it for about 2 minutes before flipping but I covered the skillet while cooking. definitely my new favorite salmon recipe

I made this and added soy sauce and garlic as another suggested. My husband all the while thinking it was going on the grill. When I told him it wasn't we put it in a container to marinate overnight. Put it on the grill in tinfoil the next day and this was OUR best meal yet with salmon. I don't usually like sweet but the soy sauce and garlic clove made it superb. I beg you to try this recipe as you won't regret it.

this was a good recipe, Ive made it three times. but.... the first time it was too sweet with the Brown sugar. second time I cut the sugar to half, but the bourbon flavor was too strong. the third tie I used the recipe as is, but only very lightly brushed it on, and baked it for 20 min til it was fork-tender. just right!!

This Salmon recipe is so delicious and easy! I served with jasmine rice and baby carrots. After removing cooked salmon from the pan I added cooked baby carrots, gave them a swirl around the pan to pick up some of the bourbon glaze and plated next to salmon. I spooned remaining glaze over the salmon. I will definitely make this again.

I made this tonight exactly like the recipe, no changes, unless you count Canadian Whiskey rather than bourbon, but since I don't know the difference that didn't matter. I melted the butter and actually let it brown since I have had browned butter over salmon and know that it gives the salmon a very good flavor. I then added the brown sugar, to the skillet, stirred until it was melted into the butter then put the salmon on top. After about 4 min I added the whiskey and stirred it in. I was afraid I was going to end up with a brittle, crunchy mass rather than a sauce, but I didn't have a problem. I turned the salmon over, cooked for a few more mins and served over wild rice. I put a bit more sauce over the meat also. I served roasted garlic asparagus as a side dish and a green salad. The sauce was sweeter than I like with salmon, so I think the next time I make it I will cut back on the sugar, may or may not add a touch of citrus juice or soy sauce, but not much. I have had many of the restaurants versions of bourbon salmon and have always liked them, but they are not quite as sweet.

I did have to taste the leftover caramel sauce, just could not resist. I think I will have to try making that and pouring it over a cake of some type (salmon-less of course). I think the sauce on it's own is yummy, just a bit too sweet for the main course.
My favorite salmon recipe. Tasty and easy to prepare
I wouldn't change a thing about this recipe!
Great recipe! I made it exactly as the recipe said, and it was perfect!
Oh my, this was so good! I was even eating the caramel - salmon caramel has an interesting flavour but I liked it. Served alongside a pea and leek pasta dish for a complete meal, yum.
